name: Employment Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Must be a highly skilled and/or qualified professional engaged by an Indian company; not available for positions where qualified Indian nationals are available, or for routine/clerical/secretarial roles.
Minimum annual salary of US$25,000 (exceptions: ethnic cooks, non-English language teachers/translators, staff of embassies/high commissions).
Sponsoring entity must be registered in India or executing a project in India (need not be the applicant's direct legal employer).
requirements.fix_path: Secure engagement by a company registered in India, or a project it is executing in India.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract / engagement letter showing salary
Proof of Indian sponsoring entity's registration/project
FRRO registration within 14 days if continuous stay exceeds 180 days

outcome.duration_length: Up to 5 years for roles under a bilateral/collaboration agreement; up to 3 years for IT-sector professionals; up to 2 years for other employment -- whichever is less than the assignment term. Extendable by state governments/FRROs up to 5 years total from initial issue.

sources.title: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India -- FAQs Relating to Work Related Visas: Employment (E) Visa criteria (highly skilled/qualified professional, not for roles where qualified Indians exist or routine/clerical work), minimum salary US$25,000/year (exceptions for ethnic cooks, non-English language teachers/translators, embassy staff), duration up to 5 years (bilateral agreement roles)/3 years (IT sector)/2 years (other), tied to assignment term, extendable to 5 years total; sponsoring entity must be registered in India or executing an Indian project

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (India). Published on tier-1 sourcing (Ministry of Home Affairs FAQ document). work_rights set to 'restricted' since the visa is tied to a specific role/engagement, not an open Indian labour-market right. family_can_join set true (dependents typically accompany on an X visa) but family_can_work set false as the conservative default -- no source in this build confirmed work rights for accompanying dependents specifically.
